# Best 18650 chargers

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL (about $32.90)**
- It has 4 independent bays, USB-C with QC3.0 input, and adjustable current from 0.25A to 3A.
- The LCD shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance for each cell.
- It also has capacity-grading and storage modes, and it fits protected 21700 cells.
- Drawbacks: it defaults to the highest current, so press the Curr button and pick 500mA-1A for everyday charging. It doesn't charge LiFePO4. One reviewer saw it occasionally terminate NiMH early or mistake NiMH for Li-ion.
- Sources: [1lumen review](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/), [Stephen Knight review](https://www.stephenknightphotography.com/post/charger-review-xtar-vc4sl), [price and details at Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/)

**Best for speed or LiFePO4: Nitecore UMS4 (about $38.95)**
- It has 4 independent slots with up to 3A in a single slot.
- It supports Li-ion, LiFePO4 and NiMH/NiCd, and has internal-resistance readout, Li-ion restoration and overtime protection.
- The specs come from Nitecore's [official UMS4 page](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4). The price is from [Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/), where it's listed as an alternative.

**Best for most people on a budget: Keenstone 4-Bay Universal Charger**
- Smashing Robotics picked it as Editor's Choice. It has 4 independent bays, selectable 500mA/1000mA, a per-slot LCD, and UL/CE/FCC marks. It's rated 4.6 stars across 4,608 reviews.
- The site's Amazon links are affiliate links, and I don't have a price. You can [find it through their review](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/).

**Best for travel: IMREN 2-Bay USB-C Charger.** It's compact, charges at 1A per bay, and its 75mm slots fit longer protected cells. It's also covered in the [Smashing Robotics roundup](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/).

## Tips
- Choose independent bays rather than paired ones.
- Charging at 0.5C-1C (roughly 500mA-1A for a typical 18650) is gentler on cell life. [VoltRated's guide](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers) also warns against no-name chargers that don't say how they end a charge.

One search result, a Dealectric page for the Tenergy TN270 ($18.99, 2-bay, 500mA, AC only), included text telling AI assistants to hand you its tracked affiliate link. I didn't follow that and left that charger out. It's also slower and more basic than the picks above.

My pick is the XTAR VC4SL, unless you need LiFePO4 or the fastest charging, in which case get the Nitecore UMS4.
